newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico arrests two alleged rebels in capital.
newsitem.headline: Mexico arrests two alleged rebels in capital.

text.p: Mexican police arrested two suspected members of the rebel Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) as they entered an underground train station armed with pistols, authorities said on Tuesday.

The Attorney General's Office said Santiago Sanchez Silvestre, 37, and Juan Garcia Cruz, 20, were seized last Friday with nine-milimeter pistols stuffed in their belts, and carrying a case that held another pistol and EPR propaganda.

The arrests took place in an underground "Metro" station in a run-down neighbourhood in eastern Mexico City the week after fighting erupted between Marxist EPR units and the army in southern Mexico in which at least nine people were killed.

Authorities have rounded up many EPR suspects in the southern state of Guerrero since those skirmishes, raising the hackles of some human rights groups who have accused the army of using repressive tactics to stifle revolt. These were the first two arrests in the capital since that fighting.

The Attorney General's Office said the two suspected rebels were preparing to distribute an EPR publication, The Insurgent. Police said they later uncovered a rebel safehouse where they found more EPR propaganda.

The two men were being held on illegal weapons charges, but the statement said they may be charged with taking part in an attack in a poor suburb of Mexico City last December in which one policeman was killed and another injured.
